title: Bullies face expulsion under new rules, says DepEd chief
summary: Students found guilty of bullying may face expulsion under a new Department of Education policy, Education Secretary Sonny Angara warned yesterday amid a reported incident involving students in Aklan.

blocks.text: Children play at the schoolyard of Diosdado Macapagal Elementary school in Quezon City in this file photo from January of this year.

MANILA, Philippines — Students found guilty of bullying may face expulsion under a new Department of Education policy, Education Secretary Sonny Angara warned yesterday amid a reported incident involving students in Aklan.

“We strongly condemn all forms of bullying in our schools. Every child deserves to learn in a safe environment, free from fear, harassment and violence. As the author of the Anti-Bullying Act of 2013 when I was a legislator, protecting children has been part of my advocacy. At DepEd, we have further strengthened this protection by updating the law’s implementing rules,” Angara said on Facebook.
Angara was referring to an alleged bullying incident involving students of Ciriaco L. Icamina Sr. National High School in Malinao, Aklan.
“Under DepEd Order 006, s. 2026, or the ESMLE Policy, we are further intensifying our response to bullying, including expulsion as a possible disciplinary sanction,” he added.

Angara urged the public to refrain from speculation and sharing unverified information, particularly photos and videos of the children involved, as the DepEd’s Aklan division investigates the incident.
“Let us not add to the trauma or put the children involved in the incident in a more difficult situation,” he said.
The secretary also vowed to hold accountable anyone found to have violated the law.
“We will continue to ensure that every school is a safe place where children can learn without fear. This is our commitment to every parent and every child in the country,” he said.
